title: Retain prepared-spill probabilistic shuffle fusion at 2 GiB
question: Can the integrated actual-spill-owner fusion justify opt-in eligibility against the original stages when output and competitor requests are matched?
summary: Linux native opt-in for the proven plain retained shape. All three pairs improved; elapsed fell 18.4%, CPU 11.5% and managed temporary traffic 32.2%. The held-peer control improves completion at three fixed points.

workloads: 2 GiB, four partition parents, stratified 80/20/0 probabilistic assignment followed by explicit Uniform, one worker, 128 MiB job and 1 GiB no-swap cgroup.
70,003 plain rows, a 32 MiB tracked shared pool, three fixed peer requests and separate fault injection.

validation.summary: Three complete pairs with exact seeded outputs and independent fields/ID/cap verification, three held-peer pairs, cancellation and pre-emission typed retry, terminal sink error and original observation indices. Feature workspace Clippy passed. One final-layout 2 GiB transfer pair preserves exactness and benefit, and all four previously affected tiny-budget controls pass.

limitations: Uncontrolled WSL2 backing cache, one worker and one timed workload.
Fixed peer requests and tested callback positions do not establish arbitrary admission-domain inclusion.
More initial runs and temporary files offset part of the traffic benefit.
exclusions: Native Windows and browser acceptance of the integrated revision and automatic/default selection.
reopen_when: Any expansion needs a workload-specific benefit and native Windows or browser acceptance of the actual integration, including observation and retained owner lifetime.
